clips.title: The story
paras: At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sends you to face Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. The hunt tests your skill and respect for nature's deadliest predators.

Sunscale raptors hunt the Barrens in cunning, vicious packs, but none inspires more dread than Speartooth. Jorn Skyseer says Ishamuhale kills by instinct and passion, not for food or territory. He hunts because killing is his nature. To face him is to test whether you can withstand a predator's unbridled ferocity.

Ishamuhale will not be found resting in a nest. To draw him out, you follow the plains' natural rhythm. Jorn tells you to kill a fresh zhevra and carry its carcass to a lone, withered dead tree on the plains northwest of Ratchet. The scent of blood on the arid wind brings Ishamuhale swiftly to claim his prey.

When you bring Ishamuhale's fang back to Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sees it as a profound spiritual milestone, not merely a sign of victory. Tauren belief holds that overcoming so fierce a predator lets you absorb some of its raw strength. The test then turns inward: you must carry that might with temperance, honor, and restraint, rather than surrender to blind bloodlust.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Ishamuhale, Speartooth, is the fiercest sunscale raptor of the Barrens. He does not hunt for sport, nor for food. He hunts because hunting is his passion. He kills because it is his nature to kill.
And you will learn of his nature, friend, for your path now follows the taloned tracks of Ishamuhale.
Begin the hunt. Slay his favorite prey, a zhevra, then bring its carcass to the dead tree northwest of Ratchet. Ishamuhale will smell the carcass and be drawn to it.

clips.title: Completion
paras: This fang is merely a token, but what it represents is profound.
Ishamuhale's strength is in you, friend. May you use it with temperance. That is your burden.
